info.title: Elegant Sip API
info.description:
Backend for the Elegant Sip storefront — single-origin Darjeeling tea.

**Money is integer paise** (1 rupee = 100 paise). Razorpay settles in paise and
floats cannot represent money. Totals are always a whole number of rupees:
GST is rounded with the same rule the storefront uses, so the figure a customer
is shown and the figure they are charged cannot drift apart.

Errors share one shape across every endpoint, modelled on RFC 9457. `detail` is
always safe to display; `requestId` ties a response to the server logs.

get.description: What the storefront may offer right now: online payment, guest checkout and the satisfaction guarantee. Never fails on a settings read; it falls back to the defaults (no guest checkout, a 30-day guarantee).
Process is running. Checks no dependencies by design.
Checks PostgreSQL and Redis, reporting each. 503 when either is unreachable, so a load balancer stops sending traffic.

post.description:
Takes a cart of product/variant/quantity and returns the authoritative money.

**No prices are accepted in the request.** Everything is priced from the catalogue,
so a tampered client cannot change what it pays. Lines the server had to change or
drop come back in `adjustments` — show them to the customer rather than silently
reconciling.

Prices and shipping are GST-inclusive (5%). `tax` is the GST contained in the total,
rounded to a whole rupee by the same shared rule the storefront uses for display.

unitPrice.description: Priced from the catalogue, never from the request

coupon.description: Null when no code was sent, or the code was rejected

couponError.description: Why the submitted code was not applied — shown to the customer verbatim

tax.description: GST (5%) contained in the GST-inclusive total, rounded to a whole rupee

adjustments.description: Lines the server changed or dropped. The UI must show these — silently altering a cart is exactly the kind of thing this storefront does not do

get.description:
Built live from the database on every request, so a price change in the admin reaches
Meta on its next scheduled fetch with no sync or redeploy.

One row per product, for the pack the product page opens on. `sale_price` is exactly
what checkout charges for one pack and is sent only when lower than `price`.
Coming-soon and retired products are omitted. Cached for 5 minutes.

post.description:
Re-prices the cart from the catalogue, reserves stock and creates a gateway order,
all in one database transaction. If any part fails, none of it happened.

The order is created as `pending_payment` and returns the gateway handle the browser
checkout widget needs. **It is not a paid order** — only a signed webhook makes it one.

No prices are accepted in the request.

post.description:
Send the three values Razorpay checkout returns on success. The signature is
checked with HMAC-SHA256(order_id + "|" + payment_id, key secret), then the
payment is looked up with Razorpay. `paid` means the order is confirmed;
`pending` means the payment is authorised but not yet captured, and the
webhook will finish it.

post.description:
Signature-verified and idempotent. **This is what confirms payment** — not the
browser redirect.

Returns 200 for any event it has safely recorded, duplicates included, because a
non-2xx would make the gateway retry a delivery that has already been handled.
A bad signature returns 401 and is not recorded.

Authenticated by the x-api-key token set in Shiprocket → Settings → API → Webhooks. Updates the shipment and moves the order to shipped / delivered. Always 200 for an accepted token so Shiprocket does not disable the hook.
Verifies the Interakt-Signature HMAC on the raw JSON body, then records sent, delivered, read, and failed status events.

post.description:
Ends the offer on one tea or on every tea, in one transaction.

`end-offer` sets the selling price to the regular (struck-out) price and clears the struck-out
price. `clear-compare-at` keeps the selling price and only removes the struck-out price.
Variants with no struck-out price are left alone. Returns what actually changed.

post.summary: Refund all or part of an order
post.description:
Refunds `amount` paise of the captured payment through the payment gateway.

Idempotent on `idempotencyKey`: repeating a request returns the refund it created (200) and never refunds twice.
The refund is recorded as pending before the gateway is asked, so concurrent requests cannot exceed the captured amount.
When confirmed refunds reach the captured amount the order and payment become `refunded`. Stock and shipments are not touched.

A gateway refusal records the refund as failed and returns 502; nothing was refunded. When the gateway gives no clear answer the
refund stays pending until its webhook arrives. `emailed` is true only when the customer email was actually sent.

post.description:
Sent by browsers, not called by the storefront. Accepts `application/csp-report`
(report-uri) and `application/reports+json` (Reporting API). Always 204; bodies
over 16 KB are rejected with 413.

post.summary: Relay a Meta Pixel event to the Conversions API
post.description:
Called by the storefront, only after the visitor accepts cookies, with the same event ID
the pixel used. A Purchase is sent only for a paid order, using its stored value and items.
Always 204; nothing is sent when the Conversions API is not configured.
